ratings_why.fun: Every turn is a wiring puzzle: slot order, gaps, Ilse before or after the King, and spend now or hold pips for the Huddle and Piper; the thin early turns keep it from an 8.
ratings_why.distinct: 8 over a 7 because the cascade belongs to the board, not the tribe: any unit, even an enemy, carries the news, so the Bad Omen turns the opponent's own board into the fuse, and no tribe today does that.

verdict_why: One real rules gap: what the Thirty-Two copies when a Blurt text carries a cap; the rest should stay as it is.

points.text: The Thirty-Two copies printed Blurt texts, but it's unclear whether the Landlady's 3-gold cap and the Cold-Shed Tangle's twice-a-turn limit come with them, or whether the copy is uncapped. Say whether a copied text keeps its limit, counted on its own or shared with the original.

Against a board that isn't Rats and has no gaps, one Bad Omen hit lights the whole touching run, so it is a board-wide burn. That's the hot part; the enemy's gaps are its only answer, so keep the gaps visible in the fight preview.
After the King's chain each unit keeps the 1 pip its later neighbour gave it, so the King quietly feeds the Hearth Huddle too. That's a bridge between spend and hold worth naming in the builds.

Point of Order keeps the unit's Gossip, so a unit at 2 Blurts and stays loaded for the next chain. A neat off-label primer for the Piper; a Rat that does this once a turn could make the hold build come together sooner.
Tiers 1 and 2 mostly add pips and small stats. One early card that changes the Blurt number, like Fips does, would bring the wiring puzzle into the first turns.

standouts.why: Points the mechanic at the enemy, and against a Piper player it backfires: a real read-the-board call.
Copies Fips's throw, the Bean-Counter's count and the Tangle's Strays on one body; slot it beside the Echo and the board turns into a new puzzle.
A one-pip hub that spreads diagonally turns the line into a star, so a gap can be bridged by where you put it.

weakest.why: A plain neighbour buff; it only fills the wire.
Generic Discover economy; once the King is out, the 5-Blurt threshold is automatic.
A vanilla starter spark with no twist of its own.

flags.note: With Fuse Attack buffs, one spark can kill every enemy in a gapless run.
A fully loaded board makes seven attacks at Start of Combat, before the enemy acts.
Whether copied texts keep the Landlady's gold cap and the Tangle's summon limit.
With the King, a free Discover every turn.
